Classifying Pureness Categorically: Well-Pointed Endofunctors specifying Monadic Idempotency in Lean 4

Hi everyone,

I've been working on classifying pureness in a general category setting, boiling down to computational referential transparency in the specific Kleisli category setting. I wanted to share a nice direct proof that formally bridges, in Lean 4, this mathematical category theory concept to a functional programming concept.

Following the definitions on nLab for idempotent monads and well-pointed endofunctors, the goal was to show that, in the pointful functional programming world, a monad M enforcing computational referential transparency (which is exactly the condition for an idempotent monad in the functional programming world) is algebraically identical to a specific endofunctor on KleisliCat M being well-pointed, where being well-pointed can be specified in the pointfree mathematical category theory world.

We formalize the monadic idempotency property (essentially map pure = pure or mx >>= fun x => pure (pure x) = pure mx) and then relate it to the corresponding well-pointedness condition of the corresponding Kleisli category.

We were able to write a single ~100-line direct proof establishing the logical equivalence ↔ by just following the monadic laws (pure_bind, bind_assoc, bind_pure_comp).

Here is the core theorem statement:

theorem idempotency_iff_well_pointed_condition :
  (∃ (wp : WellPointed (KleisliCat M) (GEF_def (κΦ M))),
    ∀ X, wp.σ.app X = fun (z : X) =>
      (pure (fun _ : PUnit.{v+1} => pure z) : M (PUnit.{v+1} → M X))) ↔ Idempotency M := by
  -- ... (direct proof using monadic laws) ...

In the forward direction, extracting the WellPointed condition allows us to directly unwrap the map and app equations into the idempotency condition. In the backward direction, we construct the WellPointed instance explicitly from the idempotency hypothesis, manually verifying the naturality and well-pointed conditions inline.

This provides a completely self-contained formal bridge connecting the mathematical categorical definition of purity with the functional programming monadic definition of computation referential transparency!

(See https://gist.github.com/LucDuponcheelAtGitHub/d845dc03ebea2755a53ee0ce34ebe7cb for a gist.)

I'd love to hear if anyone else has formalized similar correspondences or has thoughts on linking categorical endofunctor properties to functional programming patterns in Lean!
This topic was moved here from #general > Classifying Pureness Categorically by Kevin Buzzard.
